summary: Friedrich August Wolf was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (~1777–1779) and held a post at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1783–1807).

Friedrich Bechtel worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and August Fick. He served as Dozent at Göttingen (1884) and held a professorship at Halle-Wittenberg from 1895.

Friedrich Benedict Weber studied at Leipzig University (~1792–1795). He held posts at European University Viadrina (~1802–1811) and served as professor of political economy at the University of Breslau (~1811–1848).

Friedrich Bollensen was an Indologist who studied at the University of Göttingen, including Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald. His posts included teaching at Gatchina Orphanage Institute, Saint Petersburg State University, Main Pedagogical Institute, and a Sanskrit professorship at Kazan Federal University (1852–1856).

Friedrich Brockhaus was an academic who held professorships at the University of Basel (~1871–1872), the University of Jena (~1872–1875), the University of Marburg (~1875–1888), and Kiel University (~1888–1895).

Friedrich Carl Andreas worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (~1867–1868) and held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1896–1903) and the University of Göttingen (~1903–1930).

Friedrich Christian Diez was a linguist who studied at the universities of Giessen and Göttingen, and under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1818–1820). He held a long-term academic post at the University of Bonn (~1823–1876).

Friedrich Creuzer worked in religious studies, history, archaeology, and philosophy after studying at the universities of Tübingen and Jena. He held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1800–1804), Leiden University (1809), and Heidelberg University (~1804–1845).

Friedrich Delitzsch worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Ernst Windisch, Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, Hermann Brockhaus, Georg Curtius, and August Dillmann. He held posts at the University of Breslau and Humboldt University of Berlin.
Friedrich Ernst August Krause was a sinologist who studied at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin (~1904–1906). He held an academic post at Heidelberg University (~1923–1942).

Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Giessen (~1801–1803) and held posts at Giessen (~1808–1816), the University of Göttingen (~1816–1819), and the University of Bonn (~1819–1861).

Friedrich Haag worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Zurich under Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler, Göttingen, and Berlin. He taught at Zurich, Tallinn Cathedral School, Kantonsschule Schaffhausen, Gymnasium Burgdorf, and held classical philology professorships at the University of Bern (1887; 1891–1906).

Friedrich Heiler worked in religious studies and earned his doctorate from the University of Munich. He held teaching posts at Munich (1918) and the University of Marburg (1920), and served as head of the Religionskundliche Sammlung (~1927–1962).

Friedrich Hirth specialized in sinology, history, and archaeology, studying at Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald. He served in the Chinese Maritime Customs Service (1870–1897) and held the Dean Lung Professorship of Chinese at Columbia University from 1902.
Friedrich Leo was a linguist who studied at Göttingen and Bonn under Hermann Usener. He held academic posts at Bonn, Kiel, Rostock, Strasbourg, and the University of Göttingen (1889–1914).

Friedrich Majer worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Jena (~1789–1792) and under Johann Gottfried von Herder (~1795–1803), later serving as a Privatdozent at Jena (~1800–1802).

Friedrich Max Müller worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied in Leipzig, Berlin, and Paris under scholars including Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, Franz Bopp, and Horace Hayman Wilson. He held professorships in languages and comparative philology at Oxford.

Friedrich Müller worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian studies. He studied at Vienna, Göttingen, and Tübingen, learning under Anton Boller. He worked at the Vienna University Library and Austrian National Library, becoming professor at the University of Vienna in 1869.

Friedrich Nietzsche was a philosopher and linguist. He studied at Schulpforta, the University of Bonn, and Leipzig University under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl, and served on the faculty at the University of Basel from 1869 to 1878.

Friedrich Otto Schrader was an Indologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Strasbourg (~1900–1902). He served as director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (1905–1916) and became Professor of Indology at Kiel University in 1921.
